messages:
sasha: FYI we received a firm enterprise request (fintech) for per-tenant isolation + EU-only residency. They want a concrete launch plan and modest SLA language by EOW.
jia: Can we get the exact guardrails they need? e.g., do they need dedicated HW or just logical separation + KMS?
rachel: Sales note: they want tenant-scoped KMS keys, tenant routing that pins to eu-west region, audit exports to their S3, and a SLA mentioning latency bounds for critical routes.
tom: Operationally, full dedicated hardware is expensive. Recommend a two-step approach: logical isolation (soft) first, then dedicated pools if they sign capacity commitments.
olivia: Compliance asks: dataflow attestation, long-term audit retention (1y), access reviews quarterly. We'll need a pre-approved NDA template.
sasha: Agreed. Preference is hosted but with strong contractual residency & isolation lane. That reduces friction for the customer.
jia: For MVP (soft isolation) propose these features: per-tenant routing tag, per-tenant KMS binding, tenant residency flag, and per-tenant audit export. Keep dedicated pools as a follow-up.
tom: Key tradeoffs to call out: soft isolation reduces batching efficiency -> higher token cost; also KV cache hit rates will drop per tenant. We'll need explicit fallback rules when spike saturates the tenant slice.
rachel: Customer is willing to accept a modest cost premium (~+25%) but wants predictable limits and a documented failover path.
infra-bot: infra-note: tenant-slicing prototype deployed to sandbox (job 9012). Quota ticket #2301 created for pool increases.
jia: Draft launch criteria for soft isolation MVP (suggested):
- Security review complete + signed dataflow
- Compliance checklist satisfied (audit + NDA)
- 48h staged canary with 0 P1s
- Perf target: p95 < 400ms on tenant flows at expected concurrency
- Error rate < 1% sustained during canary
- Customer sign-off on cost uplift and fallback policy
tom: Telemetry we must expose: per-tenant QPS, cold-start rate, KV-cache miss ratio, autoscale steps, and per-tenant error budget burn. Add to tenant dashboard.
olivia: Also need exported access logs and an easy re-ingestion path for their auditors. We'll prepare templates.
sasha: Risk register (initial):
- Fragmentation of capacity worsening global efficiency
- Uneven regional demand causing affinity imbalance
- New blindspots in per-tenant tracing
Mitigation: allocation caps, cross-region spillover rules, and per-tenant synthetic probes.
rachel: Rollout proposal:
1) This week: requirements + acceptance criteria (owner: jia)
2) 1 week: proto routing + KMS binding in staging (owner: tom)
3) 1-2 weeks parallel: compliance + legal signoff (owner: olivia)
4) 48h prod canary at 0.5% traffic -> monitor metrics (owner: rachel)
5) Ramp to 5% then gated increases (owner: sasha)
jia: If we fast-track (cross-team prioritized), suggest 4-6 weeks to MVP. If not prioritized, 10+ weeks.
tom: Ops change: autoscaler needs tenant-aware cooldowns and the ability to pin minimum capacity per tenant to prevent noisy neighbor thrash. I'll file infra PRs.
olivia: Legal: will prepare an NDA + residency clause draft. Also will add audit export cadence options (daily/weekly) for the customer.
sasha: Action items: jia -> reqs + acceptance criteria by Thu; tom -> staging config + dashboard tiles in 1wk; olivia -> compliance + NDA draft by Thu; rachel -> customer SLA language & cost note by Mon.
infra-bot: reminder: dedicated-pool provisioning requires quota approval (ticket #2301).
rachel: We'll hold dedicated-pool commitments until they opt for reserved capacity. For now focus on soft isolation.
jia: UX question: expose isolation_level on account settings? that would simplify provisioning and legal flow.
olivia: yes: expose isolation_level = ["shared","isolated_soft","dedicated"], and include default residency settings.
sasha: OK we're meeting Fri 9am to review the requirements doc. Ping if blockers.
rachel: I'll join and will bring the commercial language.
tom: I'll post the staging checklist later today.
sasha: Thanks all. End.
